[[File:MandoFatherSon.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Mandalorian father Novoc Vevut guides his son, Ghes Orade, through the ''verd'goten''.]]
{{Quote|Your father—Great-Granddad—never even took you through the ''verd'goten?"<br />"''What's that?''"<br />"''The warrior's trial. When you become an adult at thirteen.|Mirta Gev and Boba Fett|<ref name="bloodlines">''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]''</ref>}}
The '''''verd'goten''''' was the name of the traditional rite of passage in [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture in which a Mandalorian [[Youngling/Legends|youth]] was accepted as an adult. Young Mandalorians began training in military and survival skills under the tutelage of a [[Parent/Legends|parent]], typically at the age of eight [[Standard year/Legends|years]] old. The training lasted until the child reached the age of thirteen, at which [[Time/Legends|time]] they were tested on their acquired skills in fighting and surviving with the ''verd'goten''. Upon passing the trial of the ''verd'goten'', the Mandalorian was considered legally an adult, and had earned equal treatment in Mandalorian society.<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref> It was customary for fellow Mandalorians to share a [[Alcohol/Legends|drink]] with and [[Toast (ritual)/Legends|toast]] the new Mandalorian adult upon the completion of their ''verd'goten''.<ref name="APM">''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]''</ref>

Though [[Akaavi Spar]], a [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] Mandalorian [[Gender/Legends|woman]], completed her ''verd'goten'' at the age of thirteen, she began training under [[Akaavi Spar's father|her father]] at the age of three,<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> instead of the more commonly accepted age of eight.<ref name="TMPaC" /> In [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], [[Dinua Jeban]] completed her ''verd'goten''. The young Mandalorian and her mother, [[Briika Jeban|Briika]], celebrated her ascent to legal adulthood at the [[Bar Jaraniz]] on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. Amidst their revelry, the Mandalorian passerby [[Goran Beviin]] bought the pair a round of [[Ale/Legends|drinks]] and congratulated Jeban on her coming of age.<ref name="APM" /> Years later, in the wake of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Mandalorian father [[Novoc Vevut]] trained and guided his [[Gai bal manda|adopted]] son [[Ghes Orade]] through the ''verd'goten'' on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]].<ref name="TMPaC" /><ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Mandalorian coming of age rite was first mentioned in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''. It was later identified as the ''verd'goten'' in the article ''[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]'', written by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]] and published in [[February]] of [[2006]] in the [[Star Wars Insider 86|eighty-sixth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine.
